slides.title: Rule Explorer — Computer Laboratory Access (CS)
slides.purpose: Demonstrate JSON-configured Rule Explorer for Computer Science with binary output.
onScreenText: Rule: Valid ID AND Teacher Permission

visual.altText: Diagram showing two conditions entering an AND decision box for laboratory access
visual.description: Schematic of two entry requirements feeding an AND condition.

narration.script: This preview slide demonstrates the reusable Rule Explorer engine configured purely from JSON for a Computer Science access rule.

keyIdeas: Both inputs must be true for an AND rule to output 1.
slides.teacherNote: Preview-only fixture slide p01 (not published to live CDN).

interactive.title: Computer Laboratory Access Rule
interactive.instructions: Toggle the two entry conditions to see when access is granted.
interactive.fallbackText: A student enters the computer laboratory only when they have BOTH a valid student ID card AND teacher permission.
hints: Turn both switches to Present / Granted to satisfy the AND rule.

output.explanationTrue: Both required conditions are satisfied, so entry is allowed.
output.explanationFalse: At least one required condition is missing, so entry is blocked.

slides.title: Rule Explorer — The Fire Triangle (Chemistry / Science)
slides.purpose: Demonstrate the exact same Rule Explorer engine reused for Chemistry with zero component code changes.

visual.altText: Fire triangle diagram showing Fuel, Oxygen, and Heat required for combustion
visual.description: Equilateral triangle labelled Fuel, Oxygen, and Heat.
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fffbeb"/><polygon points="400,70 210,360 590,360" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#ea580c" stroke-width="6"/><text x="400" y="255" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#9a3412">COMBUSTION</text><text x="400" y="52" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#c2410c">HEAT</text><text x="165" y="385" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#c2410c">FUEL</text><text x="635" y="385" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#c2410c">OXYGEN</text></svg>

narration.script: This slide reuses the exact same Rule Explorer engine for Integrated Science and Chemistry without writing a single line of new React code.

keyIdeas: Removing any side of the fire triangle stops combustion.

interactive.title: Combustion Conditions (Fire Triangle)
interactive.instructions: Toggle Fuel, Oxygen, and Heat to observe when combustion can occur.
interactive.fallbackText: Combustion occurs only when Fuel, Oxygen, and sufficient Heat are all present.
hints: Switch Heat ON while Fuel and Oxygen are ON to sustain combustion.

output.explanationTrue: All three fire triangle requirements are present.
output.explanationFalse: Removing fuel, oxygen, or heat prevents or extinguishes combustion.

slides.title: Code Playground — Cambridge Pseudocode Activity
slides.purpose: Demonstrate code-playground configured for Cambridge Pseudocode.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#0f172a"/><text x="400" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="26" fill="#38bdf8">Total ← 0</text><text x="400" y="255" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="26" fill="#a7f3d0">FOR Count ← 1 TO 5</text><text x="400" y="300" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="26" fill="#fde68a">OUTPUT Total</text></svg>

narration.script: Run this Cambridge IGCSE pseudocode loop to compute the sum of integers from 1 to 5.

keyIdeas: Cambridge Pseudocode runs directly in the browser AST runner.

interactive.title: Cambridge Pseudocode Sum Loop
interactive.instructions: Run the pseudocode loop to output the sum of 1 to 5 (15).
interactive.fallbackText: Adding 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 in a FOR loop produces Total = 15.
interactive.pseudocodeStarter:
Total ← 0
FOR Count ← 1 TO 5
    Total ← Total + Count
NEXT Count
OUTPUT Total

slides.title: Code Playground — Read-Only SQL Activity
slides.purpose: Demonstrate code-playground configured for read-only IGCSE SQL.

visual.altText: SQL SELECT query filtering rows from a Stock table
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#0f172a"/><text x="400" y="195" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="26" fill="#38bdf8">SELECT ItemName, Price</text><text x="400" y="240" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="26" fill="#a7f3d0">FROM Stock</text><text x="400" y="285" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="26" fill="#fde68a">WHERE Quantity < 6;</text></svg>

narration.script: Run the read-only SQL query below to list low-stock items ordered by price.

keyIdeas: Inline SQL executes strictly against isolated read-only sample tables.

interactive.title: Low-Stock Items SQL Query
interactive.instructions: Run the SELECT query to find Stock items with Quantity < 6 ordered by Price descending.
interactive.fallbackText: SELECT ItemName, Price FROM Stock WHERE Quantity < 6 ORDER BY Price DESC returns low-stock items.
interactive.sqlStarter:
SELECT ItemName, Price
FROM Stock
WHERE Quantity < 6
ORDER BY Price DESC;

slides.title: Multiple Independent Activities on One Slide
slides.purpose: Verify two interactive activities on one slide maintain completely independent state and reset controls.

visual.altText: Diagram comparing two independent rules side by side: OR alarm rule and AND photosynthesis rule
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f8fafc"/><rect x="60" y="110" width="310" height="230" rx="18" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3"/><text x="215" y="235" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">Activity A: Alarm (OR)</text><rect x="430" y="110" width="310" height="230" rx="18" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="3"/><text x="585" y="235" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">Activity B: Plant (AND)</text></svg>

narration.script: This slide renders two independent Rule Explorer activities together. Toggling or resetting one must never affect the other.

keyIdeas: Each activity has its own unique id and isolated React state.

interactive.title: Activity A: Security Alarm Trigger (OR Rule)
interactive.instructions: Trigger either the door sensor OR the motion sensor to sound the alarm.
interactive.fallbackText: The alarm sounds when either the door sensor OR the motion sensor is triggered.

output.explanationTrue: At least one sensor triggered, activating the OR alarm.
output.explanationFalse: Neither sensor is active, so the alarm stays quiet.

interactive.title: Activity B: Photosynthesis Check (AND Rule)
interactive.instructions: Toggle Sunlight and Water to check if photosynthesis can proceed.
interactive.fallbackText: Photosynthesis requires both sunlight and water (alongside carbon dioxide).

output.explanationTrue: Both sunlight and water are present for the plant.
output.explanationFalse: Without both sunlight and water, photosynthesis cannot proceed.

slides.title: Graceful Fallback — Reserved & Incompatible Configs
slides.purpose: Verify runtime fallback cards for reserved Step 4 engines and incompatible minEngineVersion without crashing.

visual.altText: Safe fallback diagram showing graceful degradation when an engine is unavailable
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fefce8"/><text x="400" y="215" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#854d0e">Graceful Fallback Demonstration</text><text x="400" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#713f12">Reserved Step 4 engines and unsupported versions degrade safely.</text></svg>

narration.script: This slide intentionally contains a reserved Step 4 engine and an incompatible engine version to prove the player falls back gracefully without crashing.

keyIdeas: Invalid or future configs never break slide rendering or narration.

interactive.title: Reserved Step 4 Engine: Linear Graph Explorer
interactive.instructions: Adjust gradient m and intercept c.
interactive.fallbackText: Increasing gradient m makes y = mx + c steeper; changing c shifts the y-intercept. (Reserved for Step 4.)

interactive.title: Future Engine Version Fallback (minEngineVersion 9.0.0)
interactive.instructions: Requires a future version of rule-explorer.
interactive.fallbackText: This activity requires rule-explorer v9.0.0, so the player safely displays this fallback summary instead.
